legend: The hallmark feature is the presence of well-demarcated microscopic foci that contain neuroblastic cells embedded in neuropil. The foci are randomly distributed in ganglioneuromatous tissue composed of Schwannian cells and maturing/mature ganglionic cells. The ganglioneuromatous component exceeds 50% of the microscopic tumour section.
The neuroblastic cells span various stages of differentiation and are dominated by differentiating neuroblasts.
The presence of neuropil in tumour foci is a prerequisite for the diagnosis. Neuropil strongly expresses synaptophysin (shown here) but is negative for S100.
The presence of neuropil in tumour foci is a prerequisite for the diagnosis of ganglioneuroblastoma, intermixed. Neuropil is negative for S100 (shown here) but strongly expresses synaptophysin.

In addition to neuropil-containing tumour foci, intermixed ganglioneuroblastoma may show clusters of ganglionic cells that do not include appreciable amounts of synaptophysin-positive neuropil (shown here) but do contain S100-positive Schwann cells. Such clusters are frequently found in maturing and mature ganglioneuromas, thus demonstrating the ongoing differentiation from a stroma-rich to a stroma-dominant tumour. Immunostaining for synaptophysin aids in the identification of neuropil in the differential diagnosis between intermixed ganglioneuroblastoma and ganglioneuroma.

Contrast-enhanced CT shows a solid, well-marginated left paraspinal mass with homogeneous enhancement. The tumour encases the left subclavian artery.
Contrast-enhanced, fat-suppressed T1-weighted image shows an avidly enhancing mass at the left lung apex encasing the left subclavian artery. The latter remains patent with normal signal void.
